coverage_note: The readable opening works the question in full detail: 'if Oscar eats Chinese food then he drinks milk' is written as C -> M, its converse as M -> C, and its contrapositive as not M -> not C. The last part of the video, which asks whether the contrapositive can be false, was past the cut.
concepts: Rename each atomic sentence with a variable before writing anything: C = 'Oscar eats Chinese food', M = 'Oscar drinks milk'.
The given conditional C -> M has converse M -> C ('if Oscar drinks milk then he eats Chinese food').
Its contrapositive is not M -> not C ('if Oscar does not drink milk then he does not eat Chinese food').
Converse and contrapositive are different objects: only the contrapositive is logically equivalent to the original.
